#001

Element uses an unsupported ARIA attribute

aria-allowed-attr  •  UF-00001
Critical axe ARIA WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

ARIA attributes that are unsupported for an element's role can expose incorrect accessibility information.

Location

DOM selector: iframe[width="100%"] .ytmVideoInfoVideoTitle | Ownership: third_party_embed | Actionability: third_party_controlled

Affected HTML 

<a class="ytmVideoInfoVideoTitle" aria-level="2" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBDcyua0dFA"><span class="ytAttributedStringHost ytmVideoInfoLink ytAttributedStringWhiteSpaceNoWrap" style="">ট্যাক্স দিন, দেশকে এগিয়ে নিন</span></a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  ARIA attribute is not allowed: aria-level="2"

axe description

Ensure an element's role supports its ARIA attributes

Recommended change

Review the reported element and remove or replace the unsupported ARIA attribute according to its semantic role.

Manual review

Required: Yes

The exact correction depends on the element's intended role.
Third-party content

This finding appears inside an embedded third-party document. The website owner may not directly control the internal markup. Review the embed configuration, integration, provider options, or whether a more accessible alternative is available.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

#002

Element uses a prohibited ARIA attribute

aria-prohibited-attr  •  UF-00002
High axe ARIA WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Prohibited ARIA attributes can cause assistive technologies to receive incorrect semantic information.

Location

DOM selector: iframe[width="100%"] #movie_player | Ownership: third_party_embed | Actionability: third_party_controlled

Affected HTML 

<div class="html5-video-player ytp-hide-controls ytp-exp-bottom-control-flexbox ytp-modern-caption ytp-livebadge-color unstarted-mode ytp-small-mode" tabindex="" id="movie_player" data-version="/s/player/b7457b7c/player_embed.vflset/en_US/base.js" aria-label="YouTube Video Player">

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  aria-label attribute cannot be used on a div with no valid role attribute.

axe description

Ensure ARIA attributes are not prohibited for an element's role

Recommended change

Remove the prohibited ARIA attribute or correct the element's role and semantics.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Inspect axe's failure summary to determine the exact attribute responsible.
Third-party content

This finding appears inside an embedded third-party document. The website owner may not directly control the internal markup. Review the embed configuration, integration, provider options, or whether a more accessible alternative is available.

#003

Text color contrast requires review

color-contrast  •  UF-00003
High axe Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: .image-container.column.col-md-3 > div > p | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<p style="font-size: 9px; margin-top:-10px">e-Return Hotline Number </p>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element has insufficient color contrast of 3.15 (foreground color: #919191, background color: #ffffff, font size: 6.8pt (9px), font weight: normal). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

#020

Embedded frame does not have an accessible name

frame-title  •  UF-00020
High axe Frames WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Users may not know what content an iframe contains when it has no descriptive accessible name.

Location

DOM selector: iframe[width="100%"] | Ownership: first_party_integration | Actionability: directly_fixable

Affected HTML 

<iframe width="100%" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/MBDcyua0dFA?si=c_0lWv5p6jHSpQin" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen=""></iframe>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element has no title attribute
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

axe description

Ensure <iframe> and <frame> elements have an accessible name

Recommended change

Add a concise title attribute to the iframe describing the embedded content.

Suggested code pattern 

<iframe allowfullscreen="" frameborder="0" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/MBDcyua0dFA?si=c_0lWv5p6jHSpQin" title="Describe embedded content" width="100%"></iframe>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

The title should accurately describe the actual embedded content.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Heading order invalid

axe description

Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct

Recommended change

Review the document outline and use heading levels according to the logical content hierarchy.

Manual review

Required: Yes

A heading-level jump is not automatically a WCAG failure. The full document hierarchy must be reviewed.

#024

Image does not have an appropriate text alternative

image-alt  •  UF-00024
Critical axe Images WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Users who cannot perceive the image may not receive the information or function communicated by it.

Location

DOM selector: li:nth-child(1) > a[href$="nbr.gov.bd/"] > img | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<img src="https://nbr.gov.bd//frontend/images/home.png" style="vertical-align: top;">

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have an alt attribute
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute
  Element's default semantics were not overridden with role="none" or role="presentation"

axe description

Ensure <img> elements have alternative text or a role of none or presentation

Recommended change

Determine whether the image is informative, functional, or decorative. Informative images should have concise alternative text describing their purpose. Decorative images should normally use alt="".

Suggested code pattern 

<img alt="[Describe the image purpose]" src="https://nbr.gov.bd//frontend/images/home.png" style="vertical-align: top;"/>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

The correct alternative depends on the purpose and surrounding context of the image.

#066

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00066
High axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .contact-info > ul > li:nth-child(4) > a[target="_blank"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a target="_blank" href="https://www.facebook.com/nbr.bangladesh">
                                                                <span style="color: #3B5998" class="fa fa-facebook-f"></span>
                                                            </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" href="https://www.facebook.com/nbr.bangladesh" target="_blank">
<span class="fa fa-facebook-f" style="color: #3B5998"></span>
</a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation

Link does not have a discernible accessible name

link-name  •  UF-00078
High axe Links WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value Level A Axe automated finding
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Screen-reader users may encounter a link without being told what it does or where it goes.

Location

DOM selector: .list > .table-striped > tbody > tr:nth-child(1) > td[align="center"] > a[target="blank"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="https://nbr.gov.bd/uploads/TransferPostingTax/08_01_0000_000_019_19_0001_24_550-2026-08-25-1787676968.pdf" target="blank" style="color: orange"><img src="/uploads/pdf.png" style="height: 40px;"> </a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix all of the following:
  Element is in tab order and does not have accessible text

Fix any of the following:
  Element does not have text that is visible to screen readers
  aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty
  aria-labelledby attribute does not exist, references elements that do not exist or references elements that are empty
  Element has no title attribute

axe description

Ensure links have discernible text

Recommended change

Provide meaningful visible link text or another valid accessible name. Icon-only links should expose a concise accessible name describing their action or destination.

Suggested code pattern 

<a aria-label="Describe link destination" href="https://nbr.gov.bd/uploads/TransferPostingTax/08_01_0000_000_019_19_0001_24_550-2026-08-25-1787676968.pdf" style="color: orange" target="blank"><img src="/uploads/pdf.png" style="height: 40px;"/> </a>

Replace placeholder text with wording that correctly reflects the real page context.

Manual review

Required: Yes

Verify the final computed accessible name in the rendered browser accessibility tree.

Reference

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: a[href="tel:09643 71 71 71"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element's background color could not be determined because it is overlapped by another element

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

color-contrast  •  UF-00146
Review axe — manual review Color contrast WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA Manual review required
View issue details and remediation

Why this matters

Insufficient contrast between text and its background can make content difficult to read for users with low vision or color-vision deficiencies.

Location

DOM selector: .has-sub:nth-child(8) > a[href="#"] | Ownership: page_content | Actionability: directly_reviewable

Affected HTML 

<a href="#">Project</a>

axe automated evidence 

Fix any of the following:
  Element's background color could not be determined due to a background image

axe description

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

Recommended change

Check the computed foreground and background colors of the affected text. Normal-sized text should generally have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, while qualifying large text should generally have a ratio of at least 3:1.

Manual review

Required: Yes

axe returned this finding as incomplete when contrast could not be conclusively evaluated automatically. Background images, gradients, transparency, overlapping elements, or other rendered styling can require manual inspection.

Reference

Open axe rule documentation
